en: Ekakanipāta, Parosatavagga (The Chapter of One Hundred and Fifty)
“Even if more than a hundred who lack wisdom were to meditate together for a hundred years, [they would not equal one person of wisdom.]”
“Better than a hundred men who lack wisdom is a single man of understanding who comprehends the meaning of what is spoken.
Thus ends the first Jātaka, the Parosata-jātaka.
